title: A Drop for the Deadline
premise: Elodie Villalobos, a financial-crimes investigator who faked their death after testifying against the Marrow Syndicate, has spent two years laundering nothing but clean money in a quiet compliance office. When a burner phone rings with the voice of their presumed-dead partner, Dario, they learn the Syndicate is staging a catastrophic 'accident' at the Harborview desalination plant to bury evidence of a new laundering network. Elodie must come back from the dead to stop it, torn between duty to the truth and love for the person they abandoned. In the end, Elodie exposes the network at the cost of their anonymity, chooses Dario over the safe life, and finds that the found family of fellow witnesses becomes their real protection.
about_author: Kestrel Voss is a former bank auditor who left finance after discovering that the most dangerous money is the kind nobody questions. They write thrillers from a coastal town where the fog rolls in on schedule, and they still can't sleep through the night.

chapters.title: Clean Hands
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. Two years into witness-protection exile, Elodie reviews immaculate ledgers by day and startles at every siren by night. A routine audit flags an anomaly too perfect to be innocent. Emotional beat: the exhaustion of invisibility and the itch of old instincts waking.

chapters.title: The Phone That Shouldn't Ring
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. A burner phone appears in Elodie's mail slot—no sender, no history. It rings. The voice is Dario's, the partner who died in the crash Elodie survived. He says one word: 'Harborview.' Emotional beat: vertigo between grief and hope.

chapters.title: Proof of Life
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. Elodie tests the voice against memories only Dario would know; he passes. He claims he faked his death too—and that the Syndicate knows Elodie is alive. Emotional beat: fury at being deceived warring with relief at not being alone.

chapters.title: The Handler's Lie
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. Elodie confronts their marshal handler, Renata, who denies everything but flinches at Dario's name. Elodie realizes the protection program may be compromised from inside. Emotional beat: the ground shifting under the only safety they had.

chapters.title: Ledger Ghosts
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. Following the money, Elodie maps shell companies flowing through Harborview's construction contracts—a laundering architecture built on their own old case files. Someone studied them. Emotional beat: violation turning into cold resolve.

chapters.title: Dario in the Flesh
chapters.summary: POV alternating Elodie/Dario. A midnight meeting at a shuttered aquarium: Dario alive, scarred, unrepentant about faking his death to draw the Syndicate away from Elodie. Emotional beat: love against duty, first collision.

chapters.title: What the Water Hides
chapters.summary: POV Dario. Dario reveals the plan: a staged 'accident' at the desalination plant will destroy records and kill the whistleblowers sheltering nearby—including the family who once hid him. Emotional beat: guilt as fuel.

chapters.title: Renata's Choice
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. Renata catches Elodie investigating off-book and offers a deal: drop it, stay protected. Elodie refuses. Renata, cornered, admits someone above her leaked the witness list. Emotional beat: loyalty vs. truth, institutional betrayal.

chapters.title: The Whistleblower House
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. Elodie visits the safe house of former Syndicate accountant Miriam Okafor and her teenage son Teo, posing as an insurance adjuster. Their warmth cracks Elodie's armor. Emotional beat: found family glimpsed before it's threatened.

chapters.title: Countdown in the Contracts
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. Decoding payment schedules, Elodie pins the 'accident' to eleven days out—the plant's scheduled pressure test. Every hour matters now. Emotional beat: dread made concrete.

chapters.title: Old Friends, New Prices
chapters.summary: POV Dario. Dario works his remaining Syndicate contacts for the saboteur's name; one friend sells him out. A near-miss ambush forces Dario and Elodie to run together. Emotional beat: trust forged under fire.

chapters.title: Teo Sees Everything
chapters.summary: POV Teo. The sharp-eyed teen spots Elodie's surveillance patterns and blackmails them gently: take me with you or I'll follow anyway. Emotional beat: unexpected alliance, humor cutting fear.

chapters.title: The Mole in the Program
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. Tracing the leak, Elodie identifies Deputy Marshal Corliss as the Syndicate's inside man—but proving it means exposing themselves to federal scrutiny. Emotional beat: the cost of truth coming due.

chapters.title: Miriam's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Miriam. Miriam reveals she kept a hidden ledger of the new network—the very thing the 'accident' is meant to erase. She entrusts it to Elodie. Emotional beat: courage passed hand to hand.

chapters.title: Interrogation of One
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. Elodie turns Corliss using his own greed, learning the saboteur's cover identity and the fail-safe timeline. But Corliss tips off his handlers mid-confession. Emotional beat: victory curdling into alarm.

chapters.title: Safe House Burning
chapters.summary: POV Teo. The Syndicate hits the whistleblower house early. Elodie and Dario extract Miriam and Teo through storm drains as the building burns. Emotional beat: terror, sacrifice, and the moment strangers become family.

chapters.title: Dead Again
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. To buy time, Elodie lets the Syndicate believe they've killed the investigator—staging their own second death with Renata's reluctant help. Emotional beat: grief rehearsed, identity surrendered willingly.

chapters.title: Pressure Test
chapters.summary: POV Dario. Inside the plant disguised as contractors, Dario and Teo locate the sabotage rig while Elodie races to cut remote triggers. The countdown begins hours early. Emotional beat: adrenaline, competence, love expressed in logistics.

chapters.title: Eleven Minutes
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. The climax: Elodie confronts the Syndicate's operations chief among the pumps, choosing to broadcast the ledger live rather than escape. The rig fails; the accident dies unpublished. Emotional beat: duty fulfilled at the price of the last hiding place.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. Federal fallout: Corliss arrested, Renata vindicated but diminished, the program rebuilt around the survivors' testimony. Elodie, publicly alive, faces the cameras they once fled. Emotional beat: exposure as liberation.

chapters.title: A Table Set for Five
chapters.summary: POV Miriam. Miriam, Teo, Dario, Renata, and Elodie share a first ordinary dinner—no aliases, no exits mapped. Found family solidifies over burnt casserole. Emotional beat: warmth earned, humor returning.

chapters.title: Sleep Through the Night
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. Months later, Elodie sleeps until dawn beside Dario, the burner phone retired to a drawer as a keepsake. A new case file waits on the desk—chosen this time, not imposed. Emotional beat: peace without forgetting.
